title: Logarithmic Minimax Rates for Contrasts of Mean Within-Unit Medians from Poisson Samples
banked_reason: Delivered tier subfield < floor field; not salvageable within scope. Math panel passes; duplicate ballast theorem remains unrepaired.
gap_reasons: The delivered approximation and positive moment-matched alternatives establish the claimed two-sided rate for both benchmarks on the same full class; there is no stale conjectural or one-sided replacement in the headline. The substantive contribution is the fixed-Poisson latent-median inverse problem, with the causal contrast obtained by fair-assignment differencing and the pointwise nonregularity result confined to the specified reference law. Peng's [Theorem 6.3](https://arxiv.org/html/2606.10096v1#S6.SS2) assumes the requisite linear expansion, so it does not already establish this primitive-class precision theorem. The attainable interval relies on a single rare count and conservative coefficient and variance envelopes, leaving useful finite-sample precision and the trial-planning interpretation quantitatively unsupported. The projected score is constrained by this gap between order-optimal attainment and usable inference, the single fixed benchmark, and supporting examples limited to analytic sanity checks. proof_attempt_summary: Derived matching (log log n/log n)^2 minimax estimation and honest connected-interval length rates for the fixed Poisson latent-median benchmark, plus pointwise root-n nonregularity. The citation blocker was repaired using the locked Mathlib Stone-Weierstrass declaration and an ordinary Hahn-Banach/Riesz proof of the Hilbert criterion; the math panel passed, but achieved subfield and score ceiling 6.7 fell below field/7.4 with no bounded in-scope improvement. F1 was never entered and no Lean module was produced; decision-referee duplicate ballast at thm:kink-pointwise-nonregularity remains unrepaired, so this archive is not fully clean.
tldr: For a randomized contrast of mean within-unit medians, the sharp minimax absolute-error risk and the sharp worst-case expected length of uniformly honest connected ninety-percent intervals are both of order \((\log\log n/\log n)^2\), with the stated bounded scale \(\rho(n)\) covering every integer \(n\ge1\). The theorem holds for every Borel latent potential-density law on the specified positive Lipschitz class \(D^2\), under independent fair assignment and independent Poisson readings of mean one, retaining all original units including zero-read units. A finite sorted-reading estimator has public bias and second-moment certificates, and legal kink-family alternatives give matching lower bounds for all original-record randomized procedures. At a specified member of the same class, the actual observation-channel adjoint also proves pointwise failure of regular root-\(n\) estimation. Armwise the latent model is a strict smooth-density submodel of Peng et al.\textquotesingle s arbitrary-measure model; the randomized all-unit Poisson channel is a changed experiment.
gap: Peng et al. formulate mean individual quantiles under sparse readings but assume the influence expansion in Theorem 6.3. Existing scalar Poisson functional approximation and generic mixture duality do not evaluate the implicit median over arbitrary positive Lipschitz outcome densities.
fill: The kernel pairs a degree-squared whole-density bias theorem with legal positive full-record matching alternatives, an observable finite estimator, and an honest connected interval. The same maintained density class governs both bounds at every recruitment size.
